configuration.top_k_source: validation_sweep 15-35, prototype consultant, no test labels

source_artifacts.command: python -m src.pipeline.common.run_pipeline --dataset ton_iot --only fusion oof prototypes top_k_sweep feedback ladder

supersedes.reason: The previous ToN prototype ladder (GNN 0.3398, LLM 0.2785, AGAF 0.4447, Loop 0.4538, 'ladder holds') does not reproduce. Re-running the unchanged code on the unchanged graph, folds and seed yields GNN 0.3271 and Loop 0.3876. The LLM and AGAF rungs reproduce to 4 decimals; only the two rungs that made the ladder hold do not. The Aug-13 oof_logits.pt artifact preserved in processed_aug06_backup/ also scores 0.3271, so 0.3398 was never obtainable from the stored artifacts.

limitations: THE LADDER DOES NOT HOLD. AGAF is the top rung; the feedback loop sits below it (-0.0547, CI [-0.1273, +0.0139], P(>0)=0.059). The gap is not significant, but the point estimate is negative and the loop is not above AGAF.

The LLM rung (0.2785) sits BELOW the GNN rung (0.3271). The whitened-prototype scorer collapses under this graph's imbalance: rare classes have 12-35 edges and a class-mean prototype over 12 samples is close to meaningless.

top_k was re-selected honestly on validation (n=23). No candidate in 15-35 reaches the previously published 0.4538; the best test value in the entire sweep is 0.3994 at n=21, and selecting that would require test labels.
Classes 3 (dos, 4 edges) and 7 (ransomware, 3 edges) remain in the graph for message passing but are excluded from the metric. A 10-class macro-F1 on this graph is not a reportable number.
Edge aggregation is label-conditioned through (src_ip, dst_ip, attack_type).
